data.title: Chickenpox (varicella) — viva
data.summary: Viral infections · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Chickenpox (varicella)** (Viral infections)_

**Q1. Why is it chickenpox?**
- Fever followed by crops of itchy lesions in different stages (macule → papule → vesicle 'dew drop on rose petal' → pustule → crust), centripetal distribution (trunk > face/limbs), mucosal involvement, scalp involvement

**Q2. Causative agent and transmission?**
- Varicella-zoster virus (HHV-3) — airborne/droplet and vesicle fluid; infectious from 1–2 days before rash until all lesions crust; incubation 10–21 days

**Q3. Difference from smallpox?**
- Smallpox: lesions in same stage, centrifugal, deep-seated, palms/soles involved, severe prodrome — eradicated 1980

**Q4. Differential diagnosis?**
- Disseminated herpes simplex/zoster, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, PLEVA (Mucha–Habermann), insect bite reactions, rickettsial pox, eczema herpeticum, impetigo, drug eruptions

**Q5. Tzanck smear findings?**
- Multinucleated giant cells and intranuclear inclusions (Cowdry type A) — same as HSV

**Q6. Complications?**
- Secondary bacterial infection (commonest), scarring, pneumonia (adults, smokers, pregnancy), encephalitis/cerebellar ataxia, Reye syndrome (aspirin), hepatitis, purpura fulminans, congenital varicella syndrome (first 20 weeks), neonatal varicella (maternal rash 5 days before to 2 days after delivery)

**Q7. Management?**
- Children: symptomatic (calamine, antihistamines, paracetamol — avoid aspirin); acyclovir 20 mg/kg four times daily × 5 days in adolescents/adults, secondary cases in households, chronic skin/lung disease
- Immunocompromised/pregnant/pneumonia: IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg 8-hourly
- Post-exposure: vaccine within 3–5 days, VZIG within 10 days for high-risk

**Q8. Vaccines available?**
- Live attenuated varicella vaccine (Oka strain) 2 doses (12–15 months and 4–6 years); MMRV; zoster vaccines (recombinant Shingrix) for adults

**Q9. Diseases caused by poxviruses (as asked in DYP)?**
- Smallpox, mpox (monkeypox), cowpox, vaccinia, molluscum contagiosum, orf, milker's nodule — chickenpox is NOT a poxvirus (it is a herpesvirus)

## Quick spotter facts
- Polymorphic crops of vesicles ('dew drop on rose petal') — varicella

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Chicken pox); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.20–21. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
